newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian stocks down as foreign funds stay away.
newsitem.headline: Colombian stocks down as foreign funds stay away.

text.p: Colombian stocks fell in busy sessions marked by a lack of demand from foreign funds, brokers said.
Bogota's IBB index dipped 0.65 percent to 1,056.42 amid a 4.6 billion peso volume. Medellin's IBOMED general price index dipped 0.54 percent to 16,674.01 amid a 3.9 billion peso trade.
"There was some price correction on some bluechip shares because of the absence of demand from foreign funds, which generally keeps their prices high," one Bogota broker said.
Brewing giant Bavaria dropped 2.22 percent to 6,600 in Bogota and fell 2.94 percent to the same price in Medellin.
Banco de Colombia fell 1.86 percent to 422 in Bogota but remained unchanged at 425 in Medellin. Cigarette manufacturer Coltabaco fell 1.31 percent to 3,750.

One of the day's biggest gainers was Bancoquia bank, up 1.18 percent to 2,985, in Bogota and up 1.69 percent to the same price in Medellin on news that a deal with Spain's Grupo Santander should be signed by April that will see Banco Santander taking a 55 percent in the Colombian bank.
Brokers reported foreign fund interest in cement manufacturer Cemento Argos, up 1.13 percent to 7,950 in Bogota and up 0.63 percent to the same price in Medellin.
